rationale: llubenchmark is a small, loop- and pointer-intensive C benchmark from the LLVM test suite (linked-list construction/traversal with heavy integer arithmetic and hot inner loops), and its empty profile confirms no call-heavy or I/O-heavy structure to exploit, so the weight table favors transformations with the best resistance-per-overhead ratio: SUB leads because instruction substitution is essentially free at runtime and directly obscures the arithmetic at the benchmark's core; FLA is weighted highest on SecurityGain/DiversityGain since control-flow flattening is the strongest structural deterrent for loop-dominated code, with a moderate RuntimeCost weight so it is steered away from the hottest inner-loop functions; BCF keeps high security weight but the lowest cost weights (0.15) because bogus control flow carries the worst runtime/size blowup and must be restricted to functions without hot-loop features; SPLIT is retained as a cheap complement that adds structural diversity with minimal risk; IBR and IGV get balanced mid-range weights to raise diversity around pointer and global accesses (the list head and node fields) without amplifying memory-latency costs; ICALL stays enabled with moderate security weights since the benchmark's few calls limit its payoff, but its low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights confine it to non-critical call sites; all CorrectnessRisk weights are kept at or below 0.30 so that selection biases application toward functions whose features indicate safety, preserving correctness while the high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights concentrate obfuscation where reverse-engineering value is highest.
